April 8, 1935.
Morning translation
STUDENTS OF A BENEVOLENT INSTITUTION ON STRIKE
The Shanghai Benevolent & Industrial Institution,
Kiaochow Road, was established many years ago by the
Shaochow Fellow Provincials' Association.
In March the students of the institution went
on strike as a protest against Dean Ching Hung Doo (金宏度).
Subsequently, Quo Shou Chen (郭守纯), President of the
institution, dismissed a number of the students.
The dismissed students have submitted a joint
letter to the Bureau of Education and the Shaochow
Fellow Provincials' Association requesting them to
support justice and to conduct an investigation into
the trouble.

晨间译件
一所慈善机构的学生罢工
位于胶州路的上海贫儿教养院（Shanghai Benevolent & Industrial Institution），系由绍兴同乡会于多年前创办。
今年三月，该院学生为抗议教务长金宏度（Ching Hung Doo）而举行罢课。
随后，该院院长郭守纯（Quo Shou Chen）开除了部分学生。
被开除的学生已向教育局及绍兴同乡会递交联名信，请求主持公道并对此次纠纷进行调查。

March 28, 1935.

Shanghai Benevolent & Industrial Institution - students
resume studies

The students of the Shanghai Benevolent & Industrial
Institution, who suspended studies on March 25 to enforce
their demand that Ching Hung-do (金宏度), the master of
discipline, be dismissed, resumed studies this morning,
March 28. The four pupils who are believed to be the
ringleaders have been dismissed, while the master of
Discipline and the school physician have tendered their
resignations to the Board of Directors of the Institution.

Shanghai Benevolent & Industrial Institution
- Students suspend studies

The students of the Shanghai Benevolent & Industrial
Institution, who suspended studies on March 25 to enforce
their demand that Ching Hung-do (金宏度), the master of
discipline, be dismissed, still refuse to resume studies
this morning, March 27.

Some thirty directors and teachers of the Institution
held a meeting on the premises at 397 Kiaochow Road, at
2 p.m. March 26, and decided to dismiss the four pupils
who are believed to be the ringleaders. Measures to deal
with the master of discipline and school physician were
shelved pending a thorough investigation into the complaint
made by the students against them.

March 26, 1935.

Miscellaneous (3)

Students of the Shanghai Benevolent and Industrial
Institution suspend studies

At 4 a.m. March 25, some 450 pupils of the Shanghai
Benevolent & Industrial Institution, 397 Kiaochow Road,
posted slogans on the walls of the institution denouncing
the master of discipline named Ching Hung-do (崔宏度).
Subsequently these pupils refused to attend classes in an
effort to enforce their demand that Ching be dismissed.
Studies are still suspended this morning, March 26. It
is learned that the students consider that the master of
discipline is too strict.

This institution is a benevolent organization depending
upon the fund raised by contributions during past years.
20 students pay a fee of sixty dollars per term, while the
others are admitted free of charge.

J. P. Giveans
D. C. (Special Branch).

（左侧批注：D6605 S）

上海贫儿教养院学生停课

3月25日凌晨4时，位于胶州路397号的上海贫儿教养院约450名学生在校内墙壁张贴标语，谴责名为崔宏度（Ching Hung-do）[注：此处英文拼写对应中文音译与前后文略有出入，前文为金宏度]的训育主任。随后，这些学生拒绝上课，以强制要求撤换崔氏。截至今晨（3月26日），停课仍在继续。据悉，学生们认为该训育主任过于严厉。

该机构是一家慈善组织，依靠过去多年募集的捐款基金维持运作。20名学生每学期缴纳六十元学费，其余学生免费入学。

Subject (in full) Report on Trouble at the Shanghai Benevolent Industrial
Institution 91 Kiaochow Road.

Made by D. S. Rhodes. Forwarded by

Sir,
At 4 a.m. 25/3/35, Mr. S.Z. Kwuah, director and
secretary of the Shanghai Benevolent Industrial Institution
(貧兒敎養院), 91 Kiaochow Road, came to the station and
reported that the scholars of the above school totalling about
450 were causing trouble in the institution grounds.
Inspector Holt i/c of the party of Police attended
and from enquiries made by the undersigned and C.D.S. 299 and
C.D.C. 225 the following was ascertained: Mr. Kwauh about two
weeks ago received information to the effect that the students
were dissatisfied with the head teacher named Ching Song Doo
(金宏度) and intended to agitate to get him removed, in conse-
quent of this information the informant has since resided on
the premises.
At about 3.30 a.m. this inst. three ring-leaders
namely, Koh Dih Zeu (郭迪瑞), Tsang Ying Mong (張英明) and Sing
Ying Zeu (鄭元善) took possession of the keys from the watchmen
locked the main gate and cut the telephone wires, they then
proceeded around all the dormitories aroused all the students
who armed with long poles attacked the school staff of teachers
and coolies. On arrival of the Police an entry was forced into
the grounds, but it was seen that the students were quite orderly
and no sign of any damage having been done was noticed.
Mr. S.Z. Kwauh was questioned re the ring-leaders
and it was learned that they had escaped and despite a search
of the building they could not be found.
The students stated that they resented the severity
of the head master Ching Oong Doo who had them expelled for tri-
vial matters and posters were found in the school grounds which

主题（全称） 关于胶州路91号上海贫儿教养院发生骚乱的报告。

报告人 D. S. Rhodes。 转呈人

敬启者，
1935年3月25日凌晨4时，胶州路91号上海贫儿教养院（貧兒敎養院）的董事兼秘书S.Z. Kwuah先生来到捕房报告称，上述学校约450名学生正在院内闹事。
负责该行动的霍尔特（Holt）巡官率警员到场，经本报告人及华籍侦探299号和华籍警长225号查询，查明情况如下：Kwauh先生约两周前收到消息，称学生对名为金宏度（Ching Song Doo）的教务长不满，并意图煽动将其撤职；鉴于此消息，举报人此后一直住在院内。
本月25日凌晨3时30分左右，三名带头人，即郭迪瑞（Koh Dih Zeu）、张英明（Tsang Ying Mong）和郑元善（Sing Ying Zeu），从看守处拿走钥匙，锁上大门并切断电话线，随后前往所有宿舍，唤醒所有学生，学生手持长杆袭击了学校的教员和苦力。警察到达后强行进入院内，但发现学生秩序井然，未发现任何损坏迹象。
经询问S.Z. Kwauh先生关于带头人的情况，得知他们已逃跑，尽管对建筑物进行了搜查，但未能找到他们。
学生表示，他们怨恨教务长金宏度（Ching Oong Doo）的严厉，他因琐事将他们开除，并在校园内发现了写有如下内容的标语
